# PRD

- **Spec:** `20_fork_patch_sync` (id `20`, name `fork_patch_sync`)
- **Title:** Fork-Authoritative Patch Branch Sync
- **Status:** active
- **Schema version:** 3
- **Created:** 2026-10-01T14:21:48.852422Z
- **Source:** https://github.com/agent-fox-dev/hub/issues/35
- **Intent hash:** `3c7be7e44f83f39ecaa575303a2df20574b32bae706859b0e340627ae52ca0d5`

## Intent

The carry-patch workflow rebuilds an integration branch from upstream HEAD plus an ordered list of patch branches. Today the hub is the only place those branches are read from, and sync never looks at the fork (`origin`). This spec lets a carry-patch workspace declare that the fork is authoritative for patch branches. In that mode, sync fetches the fork and brings every registered patch branch to the fork's tip. A defined divergence policy applies when the hub's copy and the fork's copy disagree. A patch branch that moved counts as a reason to rebuild, the same as an upstream advance. Per-branch outcomes are reported in the sync response and persisted for the patch-status dashboard. A workspace that does not opt in behaves exactly as before. The authority decision is recorded in `docs/adr/01-choose-the-authority-for-patch-branches.md`.

## Goals

- A workspace variable `PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE` selects `hub` (default) or `origin` as the authority for patch branches, and is read on every sync, so a change takes effect on the next sync without a restart.
- With `PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE=origin`, `POST /workspaces/:slug/sync` fetches `origin` and, for every registered patch whose status is `active`, `conflict` or `disabled`, does one of the following:
  - creates the local branch when it is missing;
  - fast-forwards it when the fork is ahead;
  - applies `PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY` (`replace`, the default, or `report`) when the two have diverged;
  - records `missing_on_origin` when the fork has no such branch.
- Before a replacement discards a hub-side tip, that tip is saved under `refs/hub/replaced/<branch>`.
- A patch branch that was created, fast-forwarded or replaced during sync triggers the same auto-rebuild as an upstream advance, under the same `AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC` control and queue deduplication. This includes a sync where upstream did not move.
- `last_sync_at` is updated on every completed carry-patch sync, so the dashboard shows when the fork and upstream were last checked.
- The sync response reports per-branch outcomes (`patches_synced`, `patches_diverged`, `origin_fetched`). Each patch persists its last sync state (`origin_sync_state`, `origin_sha`, `origin_synced_at`), and the patch-status dashboard shows it plus two summary counts.
- With the default `hub` source, no `origin` fetch happens, no patch ref is written, and existing sync responses gain only `origin_fetched: false`.
- Every existing API response field, patch status and job record shape is kept; changes are additive.

## Non-goals

This spec is the first of five scopes. The later scopes each get their own spec, and nothing below is built here.

- **`fork_patch_registration`**: making `POST /workspaces/:slug/patches` and `afc patch add` find branches that exist only as `refs/remotes/origin/*` or on the fork (the registration changes of the issue, PR-1 to PR-4).
- **`fork_push_control`**: `PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN`, the git server's per-ref rejection and forwarding of hub pushes in `origin` mode, the hub-mode mirror to the fork, and the `hub.patch.mirror_failed` event. Until it ships, a push to a registered patch branch on the hub is still accepted in `origin` mode. The next sync replaces it (with a backup ref) or reports it, according to the policy.
- **`patch_divergence_recovery`**: `POST /workspaces/:slug/patches/:id/reset-to-origin`, `afc patch reset-to-origin`, `replaced_sha` on `GET /workspaces/:slug/patches/:id`, rejecting pushes to `refs/hub/replaced/*`, and removing backup refs when a patch is removed or purged. Until it ships, backup refs written here are not cleaned up automatically.
- **`patch_authority_docs`**: the restructure of `docs/carry_patch_workflow.md` (Remotes table, "Where patch branches live", the fork-first Getting Started walkthrough, conflict resolution for both modes), `docs/examples/AGENTS_carry_patch.md`, and moving ADR 01 to `Accepted`.
- **Changing what sync fetches from `upstream`**, how merged patches are detected, or how the integration branch is built.
- **A fork-authoritative integration branch.** Sync never fetches the integration branch from `origin`.
- **Fetching the fork in standard-mode workspaces.** Their sync path is unchanged.
- **Bidirectional merge on divergence.** One side is replaced or reported, never merged.
- **Recording manual conflict resolutions into rerere from a fork push, webhooks from the fork's host, a built-in sync schedule, and restricting the fork fetch to registered branch names.** These are follow-ups.
- **Auto-disabling a `missing_on_origin` patch.** The status is left alone and the state is surfaced.
- **Changing `AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_PUSH` or the follow-up logic of `01_rebuild_worktree`.**

## Background

**Carry-patch sync today** (`internal/carrypatch/sync_handlers.go`, `runCarryPatchSync`, reached through `NewCarryPatchSyncHook` and `workspace.RegisterCarryPatchSyncHook`):

- It takes `wslock.TryLock(slug)` (409 `workspace_busy` otherwise) and resolves upstream credentials.
- It fetches the `upstream` remote only, through `cfg.Fetch` (`upstream.Fetch` in `internal/upstream/upstream.go`). A failure answers `502 upstream fetch failed`.
- It resolves the upstream base with `resolveUpstreamBase` and compares it to `workspaces.upstream_head_sha`.
- If upstream did not advance, it returns early with empty `patches_merged` and `rebuild_triggered: false`, and writes nothing. `last_sync_at` is therefore written only when upstream advanced.
- Otherwise it writes `upstream_head_sha`, `last_sync_at` and `updated_at`, runs merge detection over `active` patches, and enqueues a `rebuild` job unless `AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC` is `"false"`. The job uses key `slug`, group `slug:integration_branch` and `SubmittedBy` set to the caller.
- The response fields (`patches_merged`, `rebuild_triggered`, `rebuild_job_id`, `force_push_detected`) are built by `CarryPatchSyncResponse` / `asExtras` and merged by `internal/workspace/sync_handler.go` into the workspace JSON.
- `SyncAPIConfig` is wired in `cmd/af-hub/main.go`.

**Patch branches today.** The rebuild uses only `refs/heads/<branch>` in `<workspace_root>/<slug>/trunk`. After clone, the fork's branches exist only as `refs/remotes/origin/*`, and only a push to the hub's git server creates a local patch ref.

**Existing pieces this spec reuses:**

- `carrypatch.GitRunner` has `Run`, `IsAncestor` and `UpdateRef`, with the adapter in `wire.go`. `gitcmd.IsAncestor` runs `merge-base --is-ancestor` with exit-code discrimination.
- `workspace.ResolveCloneAuth(store, slug)` resolves origin credentials in the order `GIT_PAT`, then `GIT_USERNAME`/`GIT_PASSWORD`, then none. The same function backs `DefaultPushIntegrationFunc` for `REBUILD_PUSH_INTEGRATION_BRANCH`.
- `upstream.Fetch` shows the go-git fetch pattern: `repo.Remote(name)`, `remote.FetchContext` with `RefSpecs`, `Auth` and `Tags: git.NoTags`, and `git.NoErrAlreadyUpToDate` treated as success.
- Workspace variables are read through `GetVariableFunc` (`store.GetVariableValue`). An unset variable returns an error, which sync treats as the default.
- Patches live in the `patches` table (`internal/workspace/schema.go`: `createPatchesTableSQL`, with idempotent `patchFieldDDL` for added columns). The workspace package's `Patch`, `scanPatch`, `patchSelectColumns` and `patchResponse` (`patch_store.go`) back the REST patch responses. `carrypatch.SQLPatchStore` has its own `SELECT` and the `PatchStore` interface.
- Hub audit events are `audit.HubEvent` values passed to `audit.Emitter.Emit`, and event type strings are constants in `internal/audit/types.go` (`EventRebuildFollowup`).
- `handlePatchStatus` (`internal/carrypatch/api.go`) builds the dashboard from its own `SELECT` over `patches`.
- `docs/configuration.md` does not list workspace variables; they are documented in `docs/api.md` ("Workspace Variables Reference") and `docs/carry_patch_workflow.md` ("Configuration").

**Interaction with `01_rebuild_worktree` (active, implemented).** A rebuild applies patches in a worktree without holding the workspace lock. It snapshots patch tips as SHAs. After the run it enqueues a follow-up if a tip moved, unless `AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_PUSH` is `"false"`. A sync that moves a patch branch while a rebuild is running is deduplicated against the running job. The running job's own stale-tip check then covers it, under `AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_PUSH`, not `AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC`. This spec does not change that. A workspace that sets `AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_PUSH=false` and `AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC=true` can miss a rebuild for a fork change that lands during a run; the next sync that moves a patch or upstream rebuilds it.

**Problems in the issue found by reading the code, handled below:**

1. go-git's fetch does not prune stale remote-tracking refs. After the fork deletes a branch, `refs/remotes/origin/<branch>` would stay, and `missing_on_origin` could never be detected. The origin fetch must prune.
2. Auto-rebuild enqueue sits behind the "upstream HEAD has not changed" early return. A patch-only change would never reach it, so the early return moves after the patch refresh.
3. Merge detection runs only when upstream advanced. When a patch tip changes with upstream unchanged, detection must also run on the new tips.
4. Git-server pushes do not take the workspace lock. A push could land between sync's ancestry check and its ref write, so ref writes must be compare-and-swap.

## Requirements

### 1. Configuration

`PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE` is a workspace variable with values `hub` and `origin`. It is read through `GetVariable("workspace", slug, "PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE")` at the start of each carry-patch sync, after the workspace lock is taken. Any other value, an unset variable or a lookup error means `hub`. The match is exact and case-sensitive.

`PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY` is a workspace variable with values `replace` (default) and `report`, read in the same way. Any other value means `replace`. It is ignored when the source is `hub`.

Setting either variable needs no change to the variables API, because variables are free-form keys. The two variables are documented in `docs/api.md` ("Workspace Variables Reference") and in the Configuration section of `docs/carry_patch_workflow.md`. `docs/configuration.md` does not list workspace variables and is not changed.

Verification: unit tests cover unset, `hub`, `origin`, an unrecognised value and a variable-lookup error for both variables.

### 2. Origin fetch

When the source is `origin`, carry-patch sync fetches the `origin` remote of the trunk with:

- refspec `+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*`;
- no tags;
- pruning of tracking refs whose branch no longer exists on the fork;
- credentials resolved with `workspace.ResolveCloneAuth` (`GIT_PAT`, then `GIT_USERNAME`/`GIT_PASSWORD`, then none).

An already-up-to-date result is success.

Credential resolution for `origin` happens before either fetch, so a failure leaves everything unchanged. It answers `502` with the message `failed to resolve origin credentials`.

The order is: upstream fetch, then origin fetch, then upstream-base resolution, patch refresh, merge detection and the workspace update. All of this happens under the lock the sync already holds.

An origin fetch failure answers `502` with the message `origin fetch failed` and `error_type` `origin_fetch_failed`, so an operator can tell it apart from `upstream fetch failed`. The failure leaves `upstream_head_sha`, `last_sync_at`, patch statuses, persisted sync state and every `refs/heads/*` ref unchanged, even though the upstream fetch has already succeeded. The upstream tracking refs it updated are not rolled back. They are harmless, because `upstream_head_sha` is unchanged and the next sync sees the advance again.

When the source is `hub`, `origin` is never fetched and origin credentials are never resolved.

Because the fetch function and the origin-credentials resolver are injected (`SyncAPIConfig` gains `FetchOrigin` and `ResolveOriginAuth`, wired in `cmd/af-hub/main.go`), tests can substitute a counting stub. If the source is `origin` and `FetchOrigin` is nil, sync answers `500` with `origin fetch is not configured`.

Verification:
- A test shows `hub` performs zero origin fetches and zero origin credential lookups, using a counting stub.
- A test shows a failing origin fetch after a successful upstream fetch leaves `upstream_head_sha`, `last_sync_at`, patch statuses, persisted sync state and patch refs unchanged.
- An integration test with a real bare fork shows a branch deleted on the fork loses its `refs/remotes/origin/<branch>` ref after sync.

### 3. Bringing patch branches to the fork's tip

This runs only when the source is `origin`, after both fetches.

Candidates are the workspace's patches, in position order, whose status is `active`, `conflict` or `disabled`. Patches in `merged_upstream` or `deleted` are not candidates. The integration branch is never a candidate, even if a patch row has its name.

For each candidate, resolve the local tip (`refs/heads/<branch>^{commit}`) and the fork tip (`refs/remotes/origin/<branch>^{commit}`) to SHAs, then apply the first rule that matches:

1. **Fork has no such branch.** The local branch is left unchanged. State is `missing_on_origin`, action is `none`.
2. **No local branch.** Create `refs/heads/<branch>` at the fork tip. Action is `created`.
3. **Same commit.** Nothing is written. State is `in_sync`, action is `none`.
4. **Local tip is a strict ancestor of the fork tip.** Move the local branch to the fork tip. Action is `fast_forwarded`.
5. **Diverged** (neither is an ancestor of the other, or the fork tip is a strict ancestor of the local tip):
   - Under `replace`: first write the local tip to `refs/hub/replaced/<branch>`, overwriting any earlier backup for that branch. Then move the local branch to the fork tip. Action is `replaced`, and the element carries the replaced SHA.
   - Under `report`: leave the local branch unchanged. State is `diverged`, action is `none`, and both SHAs are reported.

After `created`, `fast_forwarded` and `replaced`, the state is `in_sync`, because the branch now equals the fork tip.

Ancestry is checked with `GitRunner.IsAncestor` on SHAs, not names.

Ref writes use `git update-ref <ref> <new> <expected-old>` through `GitRunner.Run`. The expected old value is the SHA resolved at the start of the step, or the all-zero SHA for a create. A push that lands between the check and the write therefore makes the write fail instead of being overwritten. Ref writes never use `checkout`, `reset` or `branch -f`.

If the moved branch is the one the trunk's `HEAD` currently points at (`symbolic-ref -q HEAD` equals `refs/heads/<branch>`), the working tree is hard-reset to the new tip afterwards (`GitRunner.HardReset(ctx, "HEAD")`), so the trunk's files match its HEAD, as the post-push reset does.

A failed ref write (including a lost compare-and-swap) stops the refresh at that patch. Outcomes already produced for earlier patches are kept and persisted. Sync still enqueues the auto-rebuild decision for branches that already moved (Requirement 4), does not update `upstream_head_sha`, and answers `500` with the message `failed to update patch branch <branch>`. The next sync starts again and sees the unmoved branches as still needing work.

A branch moved by `created`, `fast_forwarded` or `replaced` counts as "patch advanced" if the patch status is `active` or `conflict`. A moved `disabled` patch is refreshed and reported but does not count, because the rebuild skips disabled patches.

Verification: integration tests with a real fork repository and a real upstream repository cover:
- fork branch missing (rule 1);
- local branch missing (rule 2);
- equal tips (rule 3);
- fast-forward (rule 4);
- divergence under `replace`, asserting the backup ref holds the old tip and the local ref the fork tip;
- divergence under `report`, asserting the local ref is unchanged;
- the fork tip being an ancestor of the local tip (also divergence);
- the trunk's checked-out branch being moved and the working tree following;
- a disabled patch not triggering a rebuild;
- a ref-write failure persisting earlier outcomes and returning `500`.

Each case asserts the local ref, the backup ref, the response element and the persisted state.

### 4. Rebuild trigger and sync completion

The "upstream HEAD has not changed" early return moves after the patch refresh.

Merge detection (Requirement 5 of spec 16, unchanged in method) runs when upstream advanced or any patch branch counted as advanced in Requirement 3, so refreshed tips are examined. With the `hub` source it runs exactly when upstream advanced, as today.

An auto-rebuild is enqueued when upstream advanced, a patch branch counted as advanced, or at least one patch was newly marked `merged_upstream`. It is not enqueued when `AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC` is `"false"`. The enqueue payload, key, group and deduplication are unchanged, so a patch-triggered and an upstream-triggered rebuild collapse into one job. `rebuild_triggered` and `rebuild_job_id` keep their meaning, including `rebuild_triggered: false` when the enqueue is deduplicated.

When neither upstream nor any patch changed, the response is as today: empty `patches_merged` and `rebuild_triggered: false`.

`last_sync_at` (with `updated_at`) is written on every sync that completes, whether or not anything advanced, in both modes. `upstream_head_sha` is still written only when upstream advanced. On the ref-write failure path of Requirement 3, `last_sync_at` is not written.

Verification:
- A test shows a patch-only change with unchanged upstream enqueues a rebuild.
- A test shows `AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC=false` suppresses it.
- A test shows `last_sync_at` is updated on a no-change sync in both modes.
- A test shows a no-change sync still returns empty `patches_merged` and `rebuild_triggered: false`.
- Existing sync tests that assert no write on an unchanged sync are updated.

### 5. Sync response and CLI

The carry-patch sync response gains:

- `origin_fetched` (boolean, always present): `true` when the fork was fetched in this sync, `false` otherwise.
- `patches_synced` (array, present only when the source is `origin`, empty when there are no candidates). Each element is `{ "branch_name", "action", "state", "local_sha", "origin_sha", "replaced_sha" }`, where:
  - `action` is one of `none`, `created`, `fast_forwarded`, `replaced`;
  - `state` is one of `in_sync`, `diverged`, `missing_on_origin`;
  - `local_sha` is the local tip after the refresh, omitted when there is no local branch;
  - `origin_sha` is omitted when the fork has no such branch;
  - `replaced_sha` is present only for `replaced`.
- `patches_diverged` (array of branch names, present only when the source is `origin`): the branches whose state is `diverged`. It is always `[]` under `replace`.

In the standalone route's JSON body (`CarryPatchSyncResponse`) and in the extras merged into the workspace response (`asExtras`), an empty `patches_synced` or `patches_diverged` is still serialised as `[]` in `origin` mode. A zero-length slice with `omitempty` must not drop the field.

`afc workspace sync` prints these fields in the JSON it already prints and exits `0` on success even when `patches_diverged` is not empty. A new `--fail-on-diverged` flag makes it exit `3` after printing when `patches_diverged` is not empty, with a message naming the branches. With `--wait`, the exit-3 check runs after the rebuild wait finishes, and a wait failure (exit `1`) takes precedence. Exit codes `1` and `2` keep their current meaning.

Verification: handler tests cover the field presence rules in both modes, and CLI tests cover exit `0` and exit `3`, `--wait` combined with `--fail-on-diverged`, and the unchanged fields.

### 6. Persisted sync state and dashboard

The `patches` table gains three nullable columns through the existing idempotent `patchFieldDDL` mechanism. There is no backfill.

- `origin_sync_state` (`in_sync`, `diverged` or `missing_on_origin`);
- `origin_sha`;
- `origin_synced_at` (RFC 3339 UTC via `apikit.NowUTC`).

In `origin` mode, each candidate patch gets its state, the fork tip SHA (null for `missing_on_origin`) and the timestamp written during sync. `merged_upstream` and `deleted` rows have the three columns cleared. In `hub` mode, every row of the workspace has them cleared on each carry-patch sync. A hub-mode workspace never shows origin state.

Writing and clearing go through additive methods on `PatchStore`, `SQLPatchStore` and the test doubles.

The workspace package's `Patch`, `scanPatch`, `patchSelectColumns` and `patchResponse` expose `origin_sync_state`, `origin_sha` and `origin_synced_at` on every REST patch response, omitted when null. `GET /workspaces/:slug/patch-status` includes the same three fields per patch (omitted when null) and adds `patches_diverged` and `patches_missing_on_origin` to its summary. The summary counts are always present and are `0` in `hub` mode.

Verification: tests cover the migration on a database that already has a `patches` table, repeated `initSchema` runs, the response and dashboard shapes, clearing in `hub` mode, and clearing for `merged_upstream` patches. The carrypatch test helper DDL for the `patches` table is updated to include the columns.

### 7. Audit and logging

In `origin` mode, each completed sync emits one `hub.patch.sync` audit event. Its metadata is `{ origin_fetched, created[], fast_forwarded[], replaced[], diverged[], missing_on_origin[] }`, each list holding branch names. Each `replaced` outcome also emits a `hub.patch.replace` event with `branch_name`, `replaced_sha` and `origin_sha`, because it discards commits.

The events use the calling credential as actor, `resource_type` `patch` and the workspace slug. Their type strings are added as constants in `internal/audit/types.go`, following `EventRebuildFollowup`. `SyncAPIConfig` gains an optional `Audit audit.Emitter`, wired in `main.go`. A nil emitter skips emission, and an emit error is logged without affecting the sync.

In `hub` mode no `hub.patch.sync` event is emitted. The ref-write failure path still emits the events for the outcomes already produced. Replacements are logged at info level with slug, branch and both SHAs.

Verification: tests assert event types and metadata for a mixed sync, absence in `hub` mode, and that a failing emitter does not fail the sync.

### 8. Documentation

All of the following are updated in the same change, per the project steering:

- **`docs/api.md`:**
  - the sync response table and "Carry-Patch Sync Flow" (origin fetch, patch refresh, the early-return move, `last_sync_at` on every sync, rebuild on patch change);
  - the two new variables;
  - `AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC` text, which now also covers patch changes;
  - the patch response schema and patch-status fields;
  - the `502 origin fetch failed` and `502 failed to resolve origin credentials` messages;
  - the new audit events.
- **`docs/openapi.yaml`:** the sync description and 200/502 responses, `CarryPatchSyncResponse` (including the always-present `origin_fetched`), the patch schema, and the patch-status schema.
- **`docs/cli.md`:** the `--fail-on-diverged` flag and exit code `3`.
- **`docs/carry_patch_workflow.md`:** the Configuration entries for `PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE` and `PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY`, and one short note under the sync section. The note covers the two models and that, until `fork_push_control` ships, hub pushes to patch branches are replaced by the next sync in `origin` mode.

## Design Decisions

1. **Workspace variables, not columns.** Every carry-patch behaviour is a workspace variable today, and the variables API already accepts free-form keys. This avoids a workspace migration and an API change on the workspace object. It matches ADR 01.
2. **`replace` is the default divergence policy.** The point of `origin` mode is that the fork is the truth. Leaving a stale hub copy in place would keep rebuilding it. The backup ref and the dedicated audit event are the safety net, and `report` is the opt-out.
3. **The origin fetch prunes.** go-git does not remove stale remote-tracking refs on fetch. Without pruning, a branch deleted on the fork would still resolve at `refs/remotes/origin/<branch>` and `missing_on_origin` could never occur.
4. **Origin credentials resolve before any fetch.** A credential failure then leaves the workspace untouched, and the two fetches each use their own credentials. This keeps a public fork with a private upstream (and the reverse) working.
5. **`origin fetch failed` gets its own `error_type`.** The message alone distinguishes it from the upstream failure, and the type lets scripts do the same. The upstream error is left as it is.
6. **The state describes the branch after the sync, the action describes what was done.** A `created` branch is `in_sync` afterwards, and `missing_on_origin` with action `none` is a reported condition. This keeps `state` a stable three-value enum that maps directly to the persisted column and dashboard counts.
7. **Ref writes are compare-and-swap.** The git server does not take the workspace lock, so a hub push can land mid-sync. `update-ref` with the expected old value turns that race into a visible error rather than lost work. `IsAncestor` on SHAs, not names, keeps the check consistent with the write.
8. **A ref-write failure stops the refresh, keeps earlier outcomes, and still triggers the rebuild for branches already moved.** A moved branch looks `in_sync` on the next sync, so skipping the rebuild decision would lose the rebuild. `upstream_head_sha` is not written, so the next sync re-detects an upstream advance.
9. **A moved `disabled` patch is refreshed but does not trigger a rebuild.** The rebuild skips disabled patches, so a rebuild would do nothing. `conflict` patches do trigger one, since a fork-side fix is what the operator is waiting for.
10. **Merge detection also runs when only patch tips changed.** The issue requires merge detection to see the refreshed tips. Under `hub` it runs exactly when upstream advanced, so existing behaviour is unchanged.
11. **A newly merged patch also triggers a rebuild.** It changes the rebuild's input. Today this was implied because detection ran only on an upstream advance.
12. **`last_sync_at` is written on every completed sync, in both modes.** The issue asks for it in order to show when the fork was last checked, and a `hub` workspace gets the same correction. It is not written on the ref-write failure path, because that sync did not complete.
13. **`origin_fetched` is always present, `patches_synced` and `patches_diverged` only in `origin` mode.** One always-present boolean tells clients whether the fork was consulted, and the arrays do not appear in responses of workspaces that never opted in.
14. **Persisted state is cleared in `hub` mode and for merged or deleted patches.** A stale `diverged` label on a patch that is no longer considered, or in a workspace that switched back to `hub`, would mislead the dashboard.
15. **Interaction with rebuilds already in progress is left to `01_rebuild_worktree`.** Its follow-up check already notices a patch tip that moved during a run, under `AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_PUSH`. Changing that variable's meaning is out of scope, and the residual gap is stated in Background.
16. **Backup-ref cleanup and reading it back are separate.** `fork_patch_sync` writes `refs/hub/replaced/<branch>` because `replace` needs the safety net on day one. Exposing it (`replaced_sha`), resetting from it, and cleaning it up belong to `patch_divergence_recovery`.
17. **The issue is split into five specs.** It spans sync, registration, git-server push control, recovery endpoints and a documentation rewrite. Each of these can be built and tested independently, and together they exceed the limit of one spec. Sync comes first because every other part depends on `PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE` and the origin fetch.

## Verified External API

`github.com/go-git/go-git/v5` v5.19.1 is the only external package in use (go.mod, `go.sum`). Its source is outside the repository and could not be read. The signatures below come from call sites that already compile in this repository, except where marked.

| Symbol | Signature as used in this repo | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `git.PlainOpen` | `func PlainOpen(path string) (*Repository, error)` (`internal/upstream/upstream.go`) | verified by call site |
| `(*Repository).Remote` | `func (r *Repository) Remote(name string) (*Remote, error)` (`internal/upstream/upstream.go`) | verified by call site |
| `(*Remote).FetchContext` | `func (r *Remote) FetchContext(ctx context.Context, o *git.FetchOptions) error` (`internal/upstream/upstream.go`) | verified by call site |
| `git.FetchOptions` fields `RemoteName string`, `RefSpecs []config.RefSpec`, `Auth transport.AuthMethod`, `Tags git.TagMode` | all four set in `internal/upstream/upstream.go` | verified by call site |
| `git.NoTags`, `git.NoErrAlreadyUpToDate` | used in `internal/upstream/upstream.go` and `wire.go` | verified by call site |
| `config.RefSpec` | `type RefSpec string`, used in `upstream.go` and `wire.go` | verified by call site |
| `git.FetchOptions.Prune` | `Prune bool`: removes local refs that match the refspecs and no longer exist remotely | **unverified.** It is not used anywhere in the repo. The implementation must confirm it prunes `refs/remotes/origin/*` when a remote branch is deleted. The integration test in Requirement 2 is the check. If it does not, the fetch must delete the stale tracking refs itself, by listing the remote's branches. |

## Glossary

- **action**: What sync did to a local patch branch: none, created, fast_forwarded or replaced.
- **backup ref**: refs/hub/replaced/<branch>, which holds the hub-side tip discarded by a replacement.
- **candidate patch**: A patch of the workspace whose status is active, conflict or disabled, excluding any patch whose name equals the integration branch.
- **carry-patch workspace**: A workspace whose integration branch is rebuilt from upstream HEAD plus an ordered list of registered patch branches.
- **compare-and-swap ref write**: git update-ref <ref> <new> <expected-old>, which fails when the ref no longer holds the expected old SHA; the all-zero SHA is the expected old value for a create.
- **divergence**: Neither tip is an ancestor of the other, or the fork tip is a strict ancestor of the local tip.
- **fork / origin**: The remote named origin of the trunk; in origin mode it is the authority for patch branches.
- **hub**: The af-hub service and its git server; in hub mode its local refs/heads/* are the authority for patch branches.
- **patch advanced**: A candidate patch branch with status active or conflict that sync moved by created, fast_forwarded or replaced.
- **patch branch**: A branch registered in the patches table; the rebuild reads it only from refs/heads/<branch> in the trunk.
- **state**: The relationship between the local patch branch and the fork after the sync: in_sync, diverged or missing_on_origin.
- **trunk**: The workspace repository at <workspace_root>/<slug>/trunk.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Patch source and divergence policy configuration

**Rationale:** Operators opt a workspace into fork authority per workspace and must be able to change it without a restart.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] WHEN a carry-patch sync has taken the workspace lock, THE carry-patch sync SHALL read PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE and PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY through GetVariable("workspace", slug, name) on that sync, before any fetch
   → a variable changed between two syncs takes effect on the second sync without a hub restart
   Check: unit
   - setup: a recording GetVariable stub, a recording lock and recording fetch stubs
   - setup: PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE initially unset
   ```
   run(sync); setVar(origin); run(sync); assert calls[0:3]==[lock,getvar,getvar] ; assert originFetches==[0,1]
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] WHEN PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE has exactly the value "origin", THE carry-patch sync SHALL select origin as the authority for patch branches
   → the origin fetch stub is called once; the response has origin_fetched true
   Check: unit
   - setup: PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE is "origin"
   ```
   setVar('PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE','origin'); r=sync(); assert originFetch.count==1; assert r.origin_fetched==true
   ```
1. [REQ-1.3] IF PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE is unset, its lookup returns an error, or its value is anything other than the exact case-sensitive string "origin" (including "hub", "Origin" and an empty string), THEN THE carry-patch sync SHALL select hub as the authority and continue the sync
   → no error is returned to the caller and the sync follows the hub path
   Check: unit
   - setup: a table of PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE states: unset, lookup error, "hub", "Origin", "ORIGIN", "", "garbage"
   ```
   for v in rows: r=sync(v); assert r.status==200; assert originFetch.count==0; assert r.origin_fetched==false; assert 'patches_synced' not in r
   ```
1. [REQ-1.4] WHEN PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY has exactly the value "report", THE carry-patch sync SHALL apply the report policy to diverged patch branches
   → the local branch is unchanged; the element has state diverged and action none
   Check: unit
   - setup: origin mode with one diverged candidate patch
   - setup: PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY is "report"
   ```
   setVar(policy,'report'); r=sync(); assert r.patches_synced[0].state=='diverged'; assert refLocal==oldTip
   ```
1. [REQ-1.5] IF PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY is unset, its lookup returns an error, or its value is anything other than the exact string "report", THEN THE carry-patch sync SHALL apply the replace policy
   → no error is returned to the caller
   Check: unit
   - setup: origin mode with one diverged candidate patch
   - setup: a table of PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY states: unset, lookup error, "replace", "Report", "", "x"
   ```
   for v in rows: r=sync(v); assert r.status==200; assert r.patches_synced[0].action=='replaced'; assert r.patches_diverged==[]
   ```
1. [REQ-1.6] WHILE the selected source is hub, THE carry-patch sync SHALL ignore PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY
   → both responses are identical; no patch ref and no refs/hub/replaced/* ref is written
   Check: unit
   - setup: PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE unset
   - setup: PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY is "report" in one run and "replace" in another
   - setup: a patch branch that differs from the fork
   ```
   assert sync(policy='report')==sync(policy='replace'); assert refsWritten==[]
   ```

### REQ-2: Origin fetch

**Rationale:** The fork must be fetched, with stale tracking refs pruned, before patch branches can be compared with it.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] WHEN the selected source is origin, THE carry-patch sync SHALL fetch the origin remote of the trunk with refspec +refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*, no tags and pruning of tracking refs whose branch no longer exists on the fork, using credentials from workspace.ResolveCloneAuth (GIT_PAT, then GIT_USERNAME/GIT_PASSWORD, then none), and treat an already-up-to-date result as success
   → refs/remotes/origin/<branch> equals the fork tip for every branch; no tag is created in the trunk; the second call returns nil (already up to date)
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real bare fork with branches and a tag, a trunk cloned from it with origin pointing at the fork, and no GIT_PAT set (credentials resolve to none)
   - setup: a secrets store with three configurations: GIT_PAT set; only GIT_USERNAME and GIT_PASSWORD set; neither set
   ```
   FetchOrigin(ctx, trunk, auth); assert rev-parse origin/b==forkTip; assert tags(trunk)==[]; assert FetchOrigin(...)==nil
   for cfg in cfgs: assert ResolveOriginAuth(store,slug)==workspace.ResolveCloneAuth(store,slug)
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] THE carry-patch sync SHALL run, under the workspace lock the sync already holds, in this order: origin credential resolution, upstream fetch, origin fetch, upstream-base resolution, patch refresh, merge detection, workspace update
   → the recorded order is lock, origin credential resolution, upstream fetch, origin fetch, upstream-base resolution, patch refresh, merge detection, workspace update; the lock is held until after the workspace update
   Check: unit
   - setup: origin mode with a call-recording stub for every step and for the lock
   ```
   assert calls==[lock,resolveOriginAuth,fetchUpstream,fetchOrigin,resolveBase,refresh,detect,updateWs,unlock]
   ```
1. [REQ-2.3] IF origin credential resolution fails, THEN THE carry-patch sync SHALL abort before either fetch and change nothing
   → HTTP 502 with message "failed to resolve origin credentials"; upstream_head_sha, last_sync_at, patch rows and refs are unchanged
   Check: unit
   - setup: origin mode, ResolveOriginAuth returns an error
   - setup: upstream_head_sha, last_sync_at, patch rows and refs snapshotted
   ```
   r=sync(); assert r.status==502; assert r.error=='failed to resolve origin credentials'; assert fetches==0; assert snapshot()==before
   ```
1. [REQ-2.4] IF the origin fetch fails after the upstream fetch succeeded, THEN THE carry-patch sync SHALL abort the sync leaving upstream_head_sha, last_sync_at, patch statuses, persisted origin sync state and every refs/heads/* ref unchanged, without rolling back upstream tracking refs
   → HTTP 502 with message "origin fetch failed" and error_type "origin_fetch_failed"
   Check: unit
   - setup: origin mode with upstream advanced, FetchOrigin returning an error
   - setup: snapshot of upstream_head_sha, last_sync_at, patch statuses, persisted origin sync columns and refs/heads/*
   ```
   r=sync(); assert r.status==502; assert r.error_type=='origin_fetch_failed'; assert snapshot()==before; assert jobs==0
   ```
1. [REQ-2.5] WHILE the selected source is hub, THE carry-patch sync SHALL perform zero origin fetches and zero origin credential lookups
   → FetchOrigin count is 0; ResolveOriginAuth count is 0
   Check: unit
   - setup: PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE unset, counting stubs for FetchOrigin and ResolveOriginAuth
   ```
   sync(); assert fetchOrigin.n==0 and resolveOriginAuth.n==0
   ```
1. [REQ-2.6] IF the selected source is origin and SyncAPIConfig.FetchOrigin is nil, THEN THE carry-patch sync SHALL abort without changing state
   → HTTP 500 with message "origin fetch is not configured"
   Check: unit
   - setup: origin mode, SyncAPIConfig.FetchOrigin is nil
   - setup: state snapshot
   ```
   cfg.FetchOrigin=nil; r=sync(); assert r.status==500; assert r.error=='origin fetch is not configured'; assert snapshot()==before
   ```
1. [REQ-2.7] WHEN a branch has been deleted on the fork and an origin-mode sync fetches it, THE carry-patch sync SHALL remove the refs/remotes/origin/<branch> tracking ref so the branch resolves as absent on the fork
   → refs/remotes/origin/feat no longer exists; the element for feat has state missing_on_origin
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real bare fork and real upstream, trunk with refs/remotes/origin/feat from an earlier fetch
   - setup: feat is registered as an active patch
   - setup: feat is then deleted on the fork
   ```
   git(fork,'branch -D feat'); r=sync(); assert not refExists(trunk,'refs/remotes/origin/feat'); assert r.patches_synced[0].state=='missing_on_origin'
   ```

### REQ-3: Per-branch outcome against the fork tip

**Rationale:** Each registered patch branch must end a sync at the fork's tip or be reported, under one deterministic rule set.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-3.1] WHEN the selected source is origin and both fetches have succeeded, THE carry-patch sync SHALL evaluate as candidates, in position order, only patches with status active, conflict or disabled, excluding patches with status merged_upstream or deleted and any patch whose name equals the integration branch
   → patches_synced lists exactly the active, conflict and disabled branches in position order; the merged_upstream, deleted and integration-named patches have no element and their refs are untouched
   Check: integration
   - setup: real fork and upstream
   - setup: patches in positions 1-6 with statuses active, conflict, disabled, merged_upstream, deleted, and one active patch named like the integration branch
   ```
   r=sync(); assert names(r.patches_synced)==['a','c','d']
   ```
1. [REQ-3.2] WHEN a candidate has no refs/remotes/origin/<branch> ref, THE carry-patch sync SHALL leave the local branch unchanged and record state missing_on_origin with action none, leaving the patch status unchanged
   → the element has state missing_on_origin, action none, no origin_sha, local_sha set; refs/heads/feat is unchanged; the patch status is still active; the persisted origin_sync_state is missing_on_origin and origin_sha is null
   Check: integration
   - setup: real fork without branch feat, local refs/heads/feat exists, patch status active
   ```
   r=sync(); e=r.patches_synced[0]; assert e.state=='missing_on_origin' and e.action=='none'; assert 'origin_sha' not in e; assert status=='active'
   ```
1. [REQ-3.3] WHEN a candidate has a fork tip and no refs/heads/<branch>, THE carry-patch sync SHALL create refs/heads/<branch> at the fork tip with action created and state in_sync
   → refs/heads/feat equals the fork tip; the element has action created, state in_sync, local_sha and origin_sha equal to the fork tip; the persisted state is in_sync with origin_sha set
   Check: integration
   - setup: real fork with branch feat, no refs/heads/feat in the trunk, patch active
   ```
   r=sync(); assert rev(trunk,'refs/heads/feat')==forkTip; assert e.action=='created' and e.state=='in_sync'
   ```
1. [REQ-3.4] WHEN the local tip and the fork tip resolve to the same SHA, THE carry-patch sync SHALL write no ref and record state in_sync with action none
   → no update-ref call is made for feat; the element has action none, state in_sync; the persisted state is in_sync
   Check: integration
   - setup: real fork and trunk where refs/heads/feat equals refs/remotes/origin/feat
   ```
   r=sync(); assert updateRefCalls==[]; assert e.action=='none' and e.state=='in_sync'
   ```
1. [REQ-3.5] WHEN the local tip is a strict ancestor of the fork tip, THE carry-patch sync SHALL move the local branch to the fork tip with action fast_forwarded and state in_sync
   → refs/heads/feat equals the fork tip; the element has action fast_forwarded, state in_sync, replaced_sha absent; no refs/hub/replaced/feat exists
   Check: integration
   - setup: real fork where feat is two commits ahead of the hub's refs/heads/feat
   ```
   r=sync(); assert rev(local)==forkTip; assert e.action=='fast_forwarded'; assert not refExists('refs/hub/replaced/feat')
   ```
1. [REQ-3.6] WHEN a candidate has diverged (neither tip is an ancestor of the other, or the fork tip is a strict ancestor of the local tip) and the policy is replace, THE carry-patch sync SHALL first write the local tip to refs/hub/replaced/<branch>, overwriting any earlier backup for that branch, then move the local branch to the fork tip, recording action replaced, state in_sync and the replaced SHA
   → refs/hub/replaced/<branch> holds the former local tip and refs/heads/<branch> holds the fork tip
   Check: integration
   - setup: real fork and trunk where feat diverged (a hub commit and a different fork commit on a common base)
   - setup: policy replace
   - setup: real fork whose feat is behind the hub's refs/heads/feat (hub has extra commits)
   ```
   old=rev(local); r=sync(); assert rev('refs/hub/replaced/feat')==old; assert rev(local)==forkTip; assert e.replaced_sha==old
   assert isAncestor(forkTip, localTip) and forkTip!=localTip; run both policies; check refs
   ```
1. [REQ-3.7] WHEN a candidate has diverged and the policy is report, THE carry-patch sync SHALL leave the local branch unchanged and record state diverged with action none, reporting both the local and fork SHAs
   → refs/heads/feat is unchanged; no refs/hub/replaced/feat exists; the element has state diverged, action none, local_sha and origin_sha set and different; patches_diverged equals ["feat"]; the persisted state is diverged
   Check: integration
   - setup: real fork and trunk with a diverged feat
   - setup: policy report
   ```
   r=sync(); assert rev(local)==old; assert e.state=='diverged'; assert r.patches_diverged==['feat']
   ```
1. [REQ-3.8] THE carry-patch sync SHALL for any candidate, decide ancestry with GitRunner.IsAncestor on the SHAs resolved at the start of that candidate's step, never on branch names, and apply only the first matching rule in the order: fork branch missing, local branch missing, same commit, local strict ancestor of fork, diverged
   → the outcome equals the first matching rule in the order fork missing, local missing, same commit, local strict ancestor, diverged; every IsAncestor call receives 40-hex SHAs and never branch names; exactly one rule's ref writes occur
   Check: property
   - setup: a real git repository with generated commit graphs and a recording GitRunner
   ```
   for (fork,local,rel) in gen(): out=refresh(c); assert out==expected(first_match(rel)); assert all(isSha(a) for a in isAncestorArgs)
   ```

### REQ-4: Safe ref writes

**Rationale:** The git server does not take the workspace lock, so a push can land mid-sync and must never be overwritten silently.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-4.1] THE carry-patch sync SHALL write every patch ref and backup ref with git update-ref <ref> <new> <expected-old> through GitRunner.Run, using the SHA resolved at the start of the step as expected-old and the all-zero SHA for a create, and never use checkout, reset or branch -f to move a ref
   → each ref write is update-ref <ref> <new> <expected-old> through Run; the create uses the all-zero SHA as expected-old; the others use the tip resolved at the start of that step; no checkout, reset or branch -f call appears (apart from the HardReset of 20-REQ-4.2)
   Check: integration
   - setup: a recording GitRunner over a real repo with one created, one fast-forwarded and one replaced candidate
   ```
   calls=recorder.calls; assert all(c[0]=='update-ref' for c in writes); assert createCall[-1]=='0'*40; assert no c[0] in ['checkout','branch']
   ```
1. [REQ-4.2] WHEN a patch branch is moved by created, fast_forwarded or replaced and symbolic-ref -q HEAD in the trunk equals refs/heads/<branch>, THE carry-patch sync SHALL hard-reset the trunk working tree to the new tip with GitRunner.HardReset(ctx, "HEAD")
   → the trunk's working-tree files match the new tip
   Check: integration
   - setup: real trunk whose HEAD is refs/heads/feat with a clean working tree
   - setup: the fork has a new commit on feat adding a file
   ```
   r=sync(); assert fileExists(trunk,'new.txt'); assert status(trunk)==''
   ```
1. [REQ-4.3] IF a ref write fails for a candidate, including a lost compare-and-swap, THEN THE carry-patch sync SHALL stop the refresh at that patch, keep and persist the outcomes already produced for earlier patches, still make the auto-rebuild decision for branches already moved, write neither upstream_head_sha nor last_sync_at, and leave later patches unprocessed
   → HTTP 500 with message "failed to update patch branch <branch>"; the next sync sees the unmoved branches as still needing work
   Check: integration
   - setup: real fork, three candidates a, b, c where a is fast-forwardable
   - setup: a hub push to b lands after the ancestry check, simulated with a runner hook that advances refs/heads/b just before update-ref
   - setup: AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC unset
   ```
   r=sync(); assert r.status==500; assert r.error=='failed to update patch branch b'; assert rev(a)==forkA; assert jobs==1; assert ws.last_sync_at==before
   ```
1. [REQ-4.4] THE carry-patch sync SHALL count a branch moved by created, fast_forwarded or replaced as patch advanced only when its status is active or conflict, and count a moved disabled patch as refreshed and reported but not advanced
   → the disabled run moves the ref, reports fast_forwarded and enqueues no job (rebuild_triggered false); the conflict and active runs enqueue a rebuild job
   Check: integration
   - setup: real fork and upstream with upstream unchanged
   - setup: a fast-forwardable patch with status disabled in one run, conflict in another, active in a third
   ```
   for st in [disabled,conflict,active]: r=sync(st); assert r.patches_synced[0].action=='fast_forwarded'; assert r.rebuild_triggered==(st!='disabled')
   ```
1. [REQ-4.5] THE carry-patch sync SHALL for any sync where the source is hub or the policy is report, write no refs/hub/replaced/* ref and move no refs/heads/* ref of a diverged patch; for any sync where the source is hub, write no patch ref at all
   → no refs/hub/replaced/* ref exists afterwards; every diverged branch keeps its old SHA; in hub mode the recorder saw zero update-ref calls
   Check: property
   - setup: a real repository with generated patch branches, fork branches and statuses and a recording GitRunner
   ```
   for cfg in gen(): sync(cfg); assert refs('refs/hub/replaced/')==[]; if cfg.source=='hub': assert updateRefCalls==[]
   ```

### REQ-5: Rebuild trigger and sync completion

**Rationale:** A fork-side change must rebuild the integration branch exactly like an upstream advance, even when upstream did not move.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-5.1] THE carry-patch sync SHALL evaluate the "upstream HEAD has not changed" early return only after the patch refresh, so a patch-only change reaches merge detection and the rebuild enqueue
   → merge detection runs and the patch is marked merged_upstream; patches_merged lists it; with no patch change and no upstream advance, merge detection does not run
   Check: integration
   - setup: real fork and upstream, origin mode, upstream_head_sha equal to upstream HEAD
   - setup: an active patch that fast-forwards and whose new tip is already contained in upstream
   ```
   r=sync(); assert detector.calls==1; assert r.patches_merged==['feat']; r2=sync(); assert detector.calls==1
   ```
1. [REQ-5.2] WHEN upstream advanced or any patch branch counted as patch advanced, THE carry-patch sync SHALL run merge detection over active patches using the refreshed tips; with the hub source, run it exactly when upstream advanced
   → detection runs 0 times for the first and once for the second
   Check: unit
   - setup: hub mode, a counting merge-detection stub
   ```
   sync(unchanged); assert detect.n==0; sync(advanced); assert detect.n==1
   ```
1. [REQ-5.3] WHEN upstream advanced, a patch branch counted as patch advanced, or at least one patch was newly marked merged_upstream and AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC is not "false", THE carry-patch sync SHALL enqueue a rebuild job with key slug, group slug:integration_branch and SubmittedBy set to the caller, so patch-triggered and upstream-triggered rebuilds collapse into one job
   → rebuild_triggered true and rebuild_job_id set; rebuild_triggered false when the enqueue is deduplicated
   Check: integration
   - setup: real SQLite job queue, origin mode, upstream unchanged, a fast-forwardable active patch
   - setup: a caller identity
   - setup: a second scenario where a rebuild job for the slug is already queued, and a third where a newly merged patch is the only change
   ```
   r=sync(); assert job.key==slug and job.group==slug+':'+integ and job.submitted_by==caller; assert r.rebuild_triggered
   ```
1. [REQ-5.4] WHEN upstream advanced or a patch branch counted as patch advanced and AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC is "false", THE carry-patch sync SHALL enqueue no rebuild job
   → rebuild_triggered false
   Check: unit
   - setup: AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC is "false"
   - setup: a patch-only change in one run and an upstream advance in another
   ```
   setVar('AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC','false'); assert sync(patchOnly).rebuild_triggered==false and jobs==0
   ```
1. [REQ-5.5] THE carry-patch sync SHALL write last_sync_at and updated_at on every sync that completes, in hub and origin mode, whether or not anything advanced, and write upstream_head_sha only when upstream advanced
   → last_sync_at and updated_at are newer after each sync; upstream_head_sha is unchanged after the no-change syncs and updated after the advance
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace with an old last_sync_at
   - setup: a no-change sync in hub mode and a no-change sync in origin mode, then an upstream-advance sync
   ```
   for mode in [hub,origin]: sync(); assert ws.last_sync_at>old and ws.upstream_head_sha==oldSha
   ```
1. [REQ-5.6] WHEN neither upstream nor any patch changed in a sync, THE carry-patch sync SHALL return an empty patches_merged and rebuild_triggered false
   → HTTP 200 with patches_merged [] and rebuild_triggered false
   Check: unit
   - setup: upstream unchanged and, in origin mode, all candidates in_sync
   ```
   r=sync(); assert r.status==200 and r.patches_merged==[] and r.rebuild_triggered==false and jobs==0
   ```

### REQ-6: Sync response and CLI

**Rationale:** Clients and CI scripts need to see which branches moved and diverged without breaking existing consumers.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-6.1] THE carry-patch sync response SHALL include the boolean origin_fetched in every response, true when the fork was fetched in this sync and false otherwise, and in hub mode add no other field to the existing response
   → origin_fetched is false in hub mode and true in origin mode; the hub response key set equals the previous key set plus origin_fetched
   Check: unit
   - setup: hub mode response and origin mode response
   ```
   assert keys(hubResp)==oldKeys+['origin_fetched']; assert originResp.origin_fetched==true
   ```
1. [REQ-6.2] WHILE the selected source is origin, THE carry-patch sync response SHALL include patches_synced with one element {branch_name, action, state, local_sha, origin_sha, replaced_sha} per candidate, omitting local_sha when there is no local branch, origin_sha when the fork has no such branch, and replaced_sha unless the action is replaced, and include patches_diverged listing the branch names whose state is diverged (always [] under replace)
   → each element has branch_name, action, state; local_sha is omitted for a missing local branch, origin_sha for a missing fork branch, replaced_sha unless action is replaced; patches_diverged lists exactly the diverged branches; under replace patches_diverged is []
   Check: unit
   - setup: origin mode with candidates covering created, fast_forwarded, replaced, in_sync, diverged (report) and missing_on_origin outcomes
   ```
   for e in r.patches_synced: assert ('replaced_sha' in e)==(e.action=='replaced')
   ```
1. [REQ-6.3] THE carry-patch sync response SHALL serialise an empty patches_synced or patches_diverged as [] in origin mode, in both the CarryPatchSyncResponse JSON body and the asExtras map merged into the workspace response, and omit both fields in hub mode
   → origin mode JSON contains "patches_synced":[] and "patches_diverged":[] (not null, not omitted) in the body and in the extras; hub mode contains neither key in either form
   Check: unit
   - setup: CarryPatchSyncResponse and the asExtras map for origin mode with zero candidates and for hub mode
   ```
   b=json(resp); assert b.patches_synced==[] and b.patches_diverged==[]; assert 'patches_synced' not in hub.asExtras()
   ```
1. [REQ-6.4] WHEN afc workspace sync succeeds, THE afc CLI SHALL print the response JSON including origin_fetched, patches_synced and patches_diverged and exit 0, including when patches_diverged is not empty and --fail-on-diverged is absent

**Rationale:** The patch-status dashboard must show when and how each patch last compared with the fork.

   → each candidate row has the matching origin_sync_state, origin_sha (NULL for missing_on_origin) and a timestamp parsable by apikit.ParseUTC; the merged_upstream and deleted rows have all three columns NULL

   → all rows of the synced workspace have the three columns NULL; the other workspace's row is unchanged
   Check: integration

   → each patch carries the three fields, omitted when null; the summary has patches_diverged 1 and patches_missing_on_origin 1 for the origin workspace; the hub workspace summary has both counts present and equal to 0
   Check: integration

**Rationale:** A replacement discards commits, so it needs an auditable record beyond the response.

#### Criteria

   → exactly one hub.patch.sync event is emitted using the constant from internal/audit/types.go; metadata has origin_fetched true and created, fast_forwarded, replaced, diverged, missing_on_origin lists of branch names; actor is the caller, resource_type is patch and the workspace slug is set
   Check: integration

   - setup: a caller credential

1. [REQ-8.2] WHEN a patch branch is replaced, THE carry-patch sync SHALL emit one hub.patch.replace audit event with branch_name, replaced_sha and origin_sha, and log the replacement at info level with slug, branch and both SHAs
   → two hub.patch.replace events are emitted with branch_name, replaced_sha and origin_sha; the actor, resource_type patch and slug are set as for the sync event; two info log lines carry slug, branch and both SHAs

1. [REQ-8.3] THE carry-patch sync SHALL emit each event with the calling credential as actor, resource_type patch and the workspace slug, using the event type constants added to internal/audit/types.go
   Check: same as REQ-8.1
1. [REQ-8.4] WHILE the selected source is hub, THE carry-patch sync SHALL emit no hub.patch.sync event
   → no hub.patch.sync and no hub.patch.replace event is emitted

1. [REQ-8.5] WHEN a ref-write failure ends the refresh, THE carry-patch sync SHALL still emit the events for the outcomes already produced

   Check: integration
   - setup: recording emitter, a first candidate replaced and a second candidate whose compare-and-swap fails

   Check: unit

1. [REQ-8.7] IF Audit.Emit returns an error, THEN THE carry-patch sync SHALL log the error and continue the sync

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: Fork-side fix fast-forwards a patch and triggers a rebuild with upstream unchanged

1. **operator** sets PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE=origin and POST /workspaces/:slug/sync after a patch branch advanced on the fork
2. **carry-patch sync** takes the workspace lock, reads the variables, resolves origin credentials, fetches upstream then origin with pruning
3. **carry-patch sync** finds the local tip a strict ancestor of the fork tip and moves refs/heads/<branch> with a compare-and-swap update-ref
4. **carry-patch sync** persists origin_sync_state in_sync, origin_sha and origin_synced_at, runs merge detection, writes last_sync_at and enqueues a rebuild job
5. **carry-patch sync** emits hub.patch.sync and returns patches_synced with action fast_forwarded, origin_fetched true and rebuild_triggered true

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** HTTP sync handler, workspace lock, carry-patch sync, git runner and real git repositories, go-git origin fetch, SQLite patch store, job queue, audit emitter

**Setup:**

- running hub handlers with a real fork, real upstream, real trunk, real SQLite database and job queue
- PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE=origin, upstream unchanged, an active patch behind the fork's tip

**End state:**

- refs/heads/<branch> equals the fork tip
- patches_synced has action fast_forwarded, origin_fetched true, rebuild_triggered true with a rebuild_job_id
- the patch row has origin_sync_state in_sync, origin_sha and origin_synced_at
- last_sync_at is updated and upstream_head_sha unchanged
- a hub.patch.sync event is recorded and a rebuild job is queued

### PATH-2: Divergence under the replace policy keeps a backup of the discarded tip

1. **operator** POST /workspaces/:slug/sync in origin mode when a hub push left a patch branch diverged from the fork
2. **carry-patch sync** writes the local tip to refs/hub/replaced/<branch>, then moves refs/heads/<branch> to the fork tip
3. **carry-patch sync** emits hub.patch.replace with branch_name, replaced_sha and origin_sha and emits hub.patch.sync listing the branch under replaced
4. **carry-patch sync** enqueues a rebuild and returns patches_synced with action replaced and replaced_sha, and an empty patches_diverged

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** HTTP sync handler, carry-patch sync, git runner and real git repositories, go-git origin fetch, SQLite patch store, job queue, audit emitter

**Setup:**

- running hub handlers with real fork, upstream, trunk, database and queue
- origin mode, policy unset, a patch whose hub tip was pushed and diverged from the fork

**End state:**

- refs/hub/replaced/<branch> holds the old hub tip
- refs/heads/<branch> holds the fork tip
- the response has action replaced with replaced_sha and patches_diverged []
- hub.patch.replace and hub.patch.sync events are recorded and a rebuild job is queued

### PATH-3: Divergence under the report policy fails a CI sync with exit 3

1. **CI script** runs afc workspace sync --fail-on-diverged for a workspace with PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY=report
2. **carry-patch sync** detects divergence, leaves the local branch unchanged, persists origin_sync_state diverged and returns patches_diverged with the branch
3. **afc CLI** prints the response JSON, prints a message naming the diverged branches and exits 3
4. **operator** reads GET /workspaces/:slug/patch-status and sees the patch with origin_sync_state diverged and patches_diverged 1 in the summary

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** afc CLI, HTTP sync handler, carry-patch sync, git runner and real git repositories, SQLite patch store, patch-status handler

**Setup:**

- a running hub with real repositories and database, origin mode, PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY=report, a diverged patch
- the real afc CLI pointed at the hub

**End state:**

- the CLI prints the response JSON and a message naming the branch and exits 3
- the local branch is unchanged
- patch-status shows origin_sync_state diverged for the patch and patches_diverged 1 in the summary

### PATH-4: Origin fetch failure aborts the sync without changing state

1. **operator** POST /workspaces/:slug/sync in origin mode while the fork is unreachable
2. **carry-patch sync** completes the upstream fetch and then fails the origin fetch
3. **carry-patch sync** returns 502 "origin fetch failed" with error_type origin_fetch_failed, leaving upstream_head_sha, last_sync_at, patch statuses, persisted sync state and refs/heads/* unchanged

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** HTTP sync handler, workspace lock, carry-patch sync, go-git fetch, git runner and real git repositories, SQLite patch store

**Setup:**

- a running hub with real upstream and trunk, origin remote pointing at a non-existent path
- origin mode, upstream advanced, snapshot of workspace row, patch rows and refs/heads/*

**End state:**

- the status is 502 with message "origin fetch failed" and error_type origin_fetch_failed
- upstream_head_sha, last_sync_at, patch statuses, origin sync columns and refs/heads/* equal the snapshot
- no rebuild job is queued

### PATH-5: Hub-mode sync stays unchanged apart from origin_fetched and last_sync_at

1. **operator** POST /workspaces/:slug/sync on a workspace without PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE=origin and with no upstream change
2. **carry-patch sync** fetches only upstream, performs no origin credential lookup or origin fetch, writes no patch ref, and clears origin sync columns of all patch rows
3. **carry-patch sync** writes last_sync_at and returns empty patches_merged, rebuild_triggered false and origin_fetched false with no patches_synced field

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** HTTP sync handler, carry-patch sync, upstream fetch, git runner and real git repositories, SQLite patch store

**Setup:**

- a running hub with real repositories and database, PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE unset, no upstream change
- patch rows carrying stale origin columns, counting stubs on the origin fetch and origin credential resolver wired in the config

**End state:**

- the origin fetch and credential stubs are called 0 times
- no patch ref is written
- last_sync_at is updated and all origin columns are cleared
- the response has empty patches_merged, rebuild_triggered false, origin_fetched false and no patches_synced field

### PATH-6: A ref-write failure keeps earlier outcomes and still triggers the rebuild

1. **operator** POST /workspaces/:slug/sync in origin mode while a hub push lands on the second candidate branch after its ancestry check
2. **carry-patch sync** fast-forwards the first candidate and persists its outcome
3. **carry-patch sync** fails the compare-and-swap update-ref for the second candidate and stops the refresh
4. **carry-patch sync** enqueues the rebuild for the branch already moved, emits events for the produced outcomes, and writes neither upstream_head_sha nor last_sync_at
5. **carry-patch sync** returns 500 "failed to update patch branch <branch>"

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** HTTP sync handler, carry-patch sync, git runner and real git repositories, go-git origin fetch, SQLite patch store, job queue, audit emitter

**Setup:**

- a running hub with real fork, upstream, trunk, database and queue, origin mode, two fast-forwardable candidates
- a hub push to the second branch lands after its ancestry check

**End state:**

- the status is 500 with message "failed to update patch branch <second>"
- the first branch is moved and persisted in_sync
- the second branch holds the pushed tip
- a rebuild job is queued
- hub.patch.sync lists the first branch under fast_forwarded
- upstream_head_sha and last_sync_at are unchanged

### 3. Implement the patch-branch refresh engine with compare-and-swap ref writes (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-3.1, REQ-3.2, REQ-3.3, REQ-3.4, REQ-3.5, REQ-3.6, REQ-3.7, REQ-3.8, REQ-4.1, REQ-4.2, REQ-4.4, REQ-4.5

**Depends on:** 1

**Steps:**

- 3.1 Write TS-20-15, TS-20-23, TS-20-24, TS-20-25 and TS-20-28 against the new engine using real git repositories and a recording GitRunner, and confirm they fail
- 3.2 Create internal/carrypatch/patch_refresh.go with refreshPatchBranches(ctx, runner, trunk, patches, integrationBranch, policy) returning per-branch outcomes {branch, action, state, localSHA, originSHA, replacedSHA, status}, a patchAdvanced bool, and the error of the first failed ref write together with the outcomes produced so far
- 3.3 Select candidates in position order: status active, conflict or disabled, excluding any patch named like the integration branch
- 3.4 Per candidate resolve refs/heads/<b>^{commit} and refs/remotes/origin/<b>^{commit} to SHAs via GitRunner.Run rev-parse, then apply the first matching rule: fork missing, local missing (create), same commit, local strict ancestor (fast-forward), diverged (also fork strict ancestor of local); decide ancestry with GitRunner.IsAncestor on SHAs only
- 3.5 Write every ref with Run("update-ref", ref, new, expectedOld) using the SHA resolved at the start of the step and 40 zeros for a create; under replace write refs/hub/replaced/<b> first (overwriting via its own current value as expected-old, zeros if absent) then move the branch; never use checkout, reset or branch -f
- 3.6 Under report leave the diverged branch alone with state diverged; in hub mode the engine is never called so no patch ref is ever written
- 3.7 After a move, if `symbolic-ref -q HEAD` equals refs/heads/<b>, call GitRunner.HardReset(ctx, "HEAD")
- 3.8 Set patchAdvanced only for moved branches whose status is active or conflict; a moved disabled patch is reported but not advanced
- 3.9 On a failed update-ref return the outcomes so far and a typed error naming the branch, without touching later candidates

**Touches:**

- `internal/carrypatch/patch_refresh.go`
- `internal/carrypatch/patch_refresh_test.go`

- the checks of the criteria listed above exist as tests, are executable and pass
